title: Quantifier-free logic: ground literals and universal validity
summary: Use finite congruence closure and realizable truth-table rows to decide universal validity and existential satisfiability of quantifier-free matrices.
abstract: If two names denote the same object, a property cannot hold of one and fail of the other. This limits which rows of a truth table can describe an actual first-order structure. We decide whether finitely many equations, inequalities, and relation statements can hold together by checking their finite congruence closure, and construct a finite model whenever they can. Applying this test to the rows of a formula decides whether a formula without quantifiers can be true in some structure. Giving its finitely many free variables fresh constant names then decides whether an existential sentence has a model and whether a universal sentence is true in every nonempty structure. All symbols are uninterpreted; no background axioms such as the laws of arithmetic are assumed.
